data.hypothesis: A 128-target CTA with a 512-source tile may improve scheduling by providing twice as many CTAs as the measured 256-target/512-source configuration, while retaining shared source reuse across each CTA’s targets. The static shared arrays use 8,192 bytes. The performance effect requires controller measurement.
data.notes: This is one point in the tile/block sweep. The supplied history reports a correct 256/512 candidate with score 0.6469 and a correct 256/1024 candidate with score 0.6225; neither establishes the outcome for this 128/512 configuration, and no per-size breakdown is provided.
transformations: Set the source tile to 512 particles, requiring 8,192 bytes of static shared memory for x, y, z, and mass.

Set block and items_per_block to 128 to test whether a larger grid of smaller CTAs improves scheduling while preserving target-tail guards, partial-tile handling, self-interaction exclusion, and force arithmetic.
